# Openings

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

How the first seconds start: already moving, inside the problem, on a click or a number, never a fade-up or a title card. 10 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Problem pile-up, freeze, turn

`oh-pile-up-freeze-turn` · opening hooks · workhorse · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

The film opens inside the problem: cards, alerts or rows pile in faster and faster while a counter climbs, the picture freezes for a breath of true silence, and the turn hits on the downbeat.

- **Build:** Frame 0 already holds 2-3 overlapping cards. Arrival k comes gap_k = max(4, 14 * 0.88^k) frames after the previous one, so the pile accelerates, and each card rises from +40 px on SPR.firm with opacity over 8 f on E.smooth and a slight rotation of rand(k) * 6 - 3 deg. A corner counter climbs with Roll and countSteps(..., E.in) while the camera's k is multiplied by breath(prog(f, 0, end, E.in), 0.04). At peak density comes a designed freeze of at most 15 f, with the picture held and the bed and every tail cut dead; then the turn lands on the next downbeat b(...): the pile implodes on E.in, or the frame cuts to the answer. Sound: one soft tick per card, each 1 dB louder than the last, ending in the silence.
- **Timing:** 14 arrivals in about 100 f (gaps 14, 12, 11, 9.5, 8.4 ... down to 4 f); freeze of 15 f at most; turn on the next downbeat.
- **Use when:** Problem-first launches whose pain is volume: notifications, tickets, tabs, invoices.
- **Avoid when:** The pain is not about quantity, the brand film is calm, or the film already uses its one freeze elsewhere.

### Sparse intro, drop on the first hard cut

`oh-quiet-intro-drop` · opening hooks · workhorse · energy any · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

(Sound and picture.) The first ~2 s carry only light plucks or a filtered, wide pad under the opening type; the low end and the kick land exactly on the frame where the punchline card or first product shot cuts in.

- **Build:** Arrange or edit the track so bar 1 has no sub and no kick and sits about 14 dB under the body, sounding at intent from frame 0 with no fade-in across the first bar: a steady filtered bed of plucks or pad, which may step up a few dB at the half-bar. Keep it wide (side about 3 dB under mid) and narrow it on the drop (side 16-19 dB under mid). Put the first hard cut on a downbeat, for example b(2) in src/timeline.ts (frame 120 at 120 BPM). Edit the track so its entry (the first bar with kick and low end) lands on that exact frame (`track.py edit` with the start bar inside the intro and the entry on the cut), and add a kit swell 8-12 f before it only when the track has no pickup of its own. Keep the intro picture to one line or two short cards (2 words each at most) so reading fits the space; per-word ticks ride on top at a constant level.
- **Timing:** Intro 117-156 f (1.95-2.6 s); about +14 dB from intro to body; the track's entry on the cut frame (within 1 f); a swell, if any, 8-12 f before it.
- **Use when:** Almost any film that opens on type and then shows the product with a tension-and-release shape.
- **Avoid when:** Stings under 4 s, openers designed to be loud from frame 0 (live grid, macro scramble), or a drop that cannot land on a whole-frame cut.

### A click starts the film

`oh-click-starts-film` · opening hooks · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, vertical

From frame 0 a cursor is already travelling toward the one button on an otherwise bare stage; it presses, and the button floods open into the first scene.

- **Build:** C.paper stage with a single button (the product's primary action) slightly below centre. Cursor follows cursorArc(a, b, prog(f, -6, 18, E.glide), 0.2), so frame 0 is already mid-path because the clock starts 6 f before the shot. pressAt(f, 22) drives the cursor's press, and the button dips by 1 - 0.03 * hitPulse(f - 22, 2, 5). Iris starts at the press frame minus 1 (24 f, E.out in log space) from the button's centre and reveals the first scene inside it. Put the click SFX 0-1 f before the press frame, with nothing before it.
- **Timing:** Cursor arrives f18; press f22 (4 f down, 8 f recoil); iris f21-45; first scene live from f45.
- **Use when:** UI walkthroughs and feature films where a single action is the product ('one click to ...').
- **Avoid when:** Products that act on their own, or films where the cursor never returns after the hook (it breaks continuity).

### Cursor into a field, two-stage push, typed provocation

`oh-cursor-search-push` · opening hooks · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A small search pill sits still on a dark stage; a text cursor drifts in, the camera pushes in twice to a macro framing, and a provocative query types into the field before any brand appears.

- **Build:** Lay out the pill as world content under the anchor camera (camera(lc(A, B, t)) from src/lib/camera.ts), anchored on the caret. An I-beam SVG, placed by transform only as Cursor is, is already travelling on frame 0: it arrives on cursorArc (bow 0.2) over 30 f on E.glide, with a soft offset shadow (a copy blurred 6 px at 35% black, offset about a quarter of its height). The camera holds for the first 24 f, then push 1 takes k from 1 to 2.16 over 42 f on E.cam and push 2 from 2.16 to 7.2 over 44 f on E.glide (lc mixes k in log space, so the zoom rate stays even). Start TypeOn (cps 30) at about 60% of push 2 and feed typeOn's followX into the camera anchor through a 6-10 f lag so the camera tracks the caret without stepping; size the pill so one character advances at most 40 px on screen at 7.2x, which keeps the caret-following scroll of the typed text under 20 px/f. Draw no halo around the pill. Sound: micro ticks only (2-6 ms bursts high-passed above 4 kHz, at most one per word, 18-24 dB under the bed, with 20% seeded jitter in timing and gain), muted once the drums enter.
- **Timing:** Camera still for 24 f while the cursor flies in from frame 0 (30 f on E.glide); push 1 42 f (f24-66, peak 0.077 ln k per frame); push 2 44 f (f66-110, peak 0.082 ln k per frame); 7.2x in total over 88 f; typing from about f92 at 30 characters/s, each character at most 40 px wide on screen.
- **Use when:** AI, search or command products, or any opener whose hook is a question the product answers.
- **Avoid when:** The product has no input field, the film's camera grammar is flat, or the query runs past about 40 characters (the macro framing cannot hold it).

### Cut in mid-sentence, pull back to the line

`oh-cropped-word-pull-back` · opening hooks · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

The film opens inside one giant word, its first letter cropped by the frame edge as if cutting into a thought mid-sentence; after a beat the camera pulls back to reveal the whole sentence at reading size.

- **Build:** Lay out the whole sentence once at display size (TYPE.display, 120 px) as world content and frame shot A at k = 3.2 on the key word, offset so its first glyph is about 40% cropped by the left edge. Frame 0 is already settling: a vertical inertia(f, 0, 3, 0.8) of about 13 px, then a 0.3 px/f drift through a 36 f hold. Pull back with lc(A, B, prog(f, 36, 92, E.dolly)) to k = 1 with the sentence centred; the log-space zoom keeps the rate even, and glyphs 600 px from the anchor stay under about 20 px/f. The neighbouring words exist from the start with no fades and simply enter the frame as it widens.
- **Timing:** Settle 12 f; hold 36 f; pull-back 56 f from 3.2x to 1x on E.dolly (peak about 0.032 ln k per frame).
- **Use when:** Copy-led launches built on one charged word, in calm-to-medium films.
- **Avoid when:** The key word is short or ordinary (the crop will not intrigue), or the film already opens on another zoom-out (icon card, macro number).

### Finished result first, then rewind

`oh-result-first-rewind` · opening hooks · accent · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

The film opens on the finished end state at its most impressive, holds for a beat, then visibly rewinds every element back to the empty start, where the story begins playing forward.

- **Build:** Every element is a function of frame, so remap time once at the act root: local = f < r0 ? T_end : T_end - (T_end - T_0) * prog(f, r0, r0 + R, E.smooth), with R = 36-48 f. Pass local to every component and decide discrete state with fd(local); entrances then replay backwards, and E.out arrivals become accelerating exits. Open at T_end with breath (+2.5%) over a 40 f hold. The rewind's peak rate is 2.86 × (T_end − T_0) / R times real time, so rewind at most about 120 f of build (about 8x at the peak for R = 42); for a longer build, set T_0 to a later, partly built state. Any element whose reversed move would pass 60 px/f, and any readable text that would pass 20 px/f, fades out over the rewind instead of travelling. Put one short filtered reverse swish under the rewind and a click on its last frame, then play the walkthrough forward from T_0 on the next beat.
- **Timing:** Hold 40 f; rewind 36-48 f on E.smooth (peak about 8x real time, at most about 120 f of build); forward play from the next beat.
- **Use when:** Walkthroughs and feature films whose output is visually rich and readable at a glance.
- **Avoid when:** An end state that needs explaining, or more than about 30 state changes (the rewind turns to mush).

### Mark builds, then is thrown into a macro of itself

`oh-mark-build-and-throw` · opening hooks · accent · energy high · sting

On frame 1 a dot swells into the brand mark. The mark grows briefly, holds for a breath, then shrinks away faster and faster and hard-cuts at peak speed to a frame-filling macro of the same mark, which keeps pulling back.

- **Build:** Show the mark only; the wordmark lockup is kept for the end. A 12 px dot at frame centre scales into the 320 px mark over 18 f on E.out, while a wrapper grows 0.83 -> 1 on E.out over 32 f from f8; then hold 8 f. Exit: wrapper scale 1 -> 0.55 over 20 f on E.in, with the hard cut on the exit's last (fastest) frame. The next shot opens on the same mark at the same screen point, its k multiplied by zoomHandoff(t, v0, 24) with v0 = zoomSpeed(kOut, cut - 1) (about -0.168): it starts near 2.2x and slows to 1x with no speed step at the cut, revealing the stage and the first UI as it settles. No overshoot anywhere; the master's motion-blur pass handles the fast frames (incoming edges peak at about 59 px/f).
- **Timing:** Dot to mark 18 f on E.out (edge about 49 px/f on its first frame); grow 32 f from f8; hold 8 f (f40-48); exit 20 f on E.in (f48-68), cut at f68 (1.13 s); macro pull-back 24 f through zoomHandoff from about 2.2x.
- **Use when:** A brand-first logo sting where recognition must land in under half a second and the energy must pour into the next shot.
- **Avoid when:** The mark is unfamiliar and needs a longer hold to be learned, or the film already uses a scale-continuity cut elsewhere. Never use it to show the full lockup.

### Four live cells from frame 2

`oh-live-grid-cold-open` · opening hooks · signature · energy high · loop, launch, feature

There is no title. The film opens on a flush 2x2 grid where every cell is already mid-action (a line assembling, a counter ticking, an object orbiting, a pin dropping), so from its first frames the frame reads as one living system.

- **Build:** Root AbsoluteFill with a CSS grid (grid-template 1fr 1fr / 1fr 1fr, gap 0); every cell is overflow:hidden on the same stage colour (C.ink), so the seams disappear, with its content on the cell's own optical centre at 50-90% of the cell's width. Render each cell's scene at full 1920x1080 inside a wrapper with scale(0.5) and transformOrigin '0 0', so type keeps its native sizing and a cell can later go full-frame sharp. Wrap each cell's composition in Remotion <Loop durationInFrames={P}> with mutually awkward periods so the four never repeat in sync, and start each cell's first arrival by frame 2-6 on its own E.out curve with no shared global ease: for example a line converging with SPR.word, a Roll counter driven by countSteps(..., E.out), and an orbit whose angular speed decays as w = 11.25*e^(-t/10) + 2 deg/f, with satellites spawning on f10, f18 and f28. Only the one story element in each cell (pin, payoff word, button) gets C.accent; everything else stays greyscale. Merge every cell's cut frames into one list and nudge apart any two that fall within 6 f, and use no per-event SFX: the track carries the sound.
- **Timing:** First arrivals on f2, f2, f2 and f6 (no cell later than f8). Typical entrances: a type lockup settles in 18 f on E.out, a counter finishes in 28 f. Loop periods 260 / 462 / 244 / 428 f. Something changes somewhere about every 20 f (longest gap about 62 f). Cells 960x540 at 1080p.
- **Use when:** A hero or social loop that must show several features at once, or a launch whose first second has to prove breadth.
- **Avoid when:** The story needs one idea at a time, a single-message sting, or a 9:16 frame where the cells would shrink below about 540 px wide.

### Macro number scramble, one-frame snap-out

`oh-macro-scramble-snap-out` · opening hooks · signature · energy high · launch, sting, feature, vertical

Huge digits fill and overflow the frame, re-rolling every frame. On one frame the view cuts back to the whole figure, which rolls into the final metric and holds: the number is the hook before any brand appears.

- **Build:** Lay out the final figure once with typeStyle('display') (tabular figures, fixed group separator) at a size where the whole string spans about 0.9 W, and draw each digit column as a Roll-style strip whose mask stays 1.6 lines tall during the macro phase, so outgoing digits stack and overflow vertically. Macro phase: scale the wrapper to 1.22 about the frame centre and, on every whole frame (fd), give 1-2 columns a new digit from rand(`${seed}:${fd(frame)}`). Snap: on a single frame decided with fd (so the motion-blur sub-samples agree), cut the scale to 1.0 with no tween, clip the masks to one line and lock the columns left to right 3 f apart until the final string is forced; then hold on breath (scale +0.065%/f) with no glints or sparkles, and keep the brand out until the end lockup. Sound: five dry glitch ticks inside the first 0.6 s, then the edit puts the track's own stop on the lock frame, so the bed falls away within a frame and the hold sits in the gap; reuse the identical tick cluster under the closing sting as a bookend.
- **Timing:** Macro 29 f; snap 1 f at f29; settle 12 f; final string forced from f41 (0.68 s); hold 72 f with only the scale drift. Ticks at about 0.17, 0.23, 0.31, 0.36 and 0.40 s.
- **Use when:** The strongest proof is one metric (users, hours saved, uptime) and the film earns attention with the outcome before the brand.
- **Avoid when:** There is no credible or impressive number, or the tone is calm and premium.

### Oversize line flies through, restarts small

`oh-oversize-fly-then-small` · opening hooks · signature · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

A huge fragment of the headline, about a quarter of frame height, brakes in from the right with its letters fading on as it slows, then dissolves; three frames later the same line restarts small and centred so it can be read.

- **Build:** Start the big line's clock 6 f before the film's first frame (t = f + 6), so frame 0 already shows its first letters fading on as it brakes. Layer 1: the line at about 270 px, weight 500, colour rgba(255,255,255,0.65) on C.ink (or over a single-hue wash), with x = startX + inertia(t, 0, -70, 0.89).x (601 px of travel from 70 px/f). Per-character opacity is 0.65 * prog(t, 6 + 1.5i, 12 + 1.5i, E.smooth), so letters only resolve once the speed drops below about 20 px/f, and the whole layer fades 1 -> 0 over its last 7 f on E.smooth while it is still sliding. Start layer 2 on the next frame, with no empty frames between: a dissolve to an empty frame and a fresh start reads as the film restarting. Layer 2: the same line at reading size with its final centred layout precomputed, per-character opacity prog(t, 1.3i, 1.3i + 5, E.smooth), and container x = inertia(t, 0, -10.8, 0.88).x: an 84 px drift that lands exactly centred and never passes 12 px/f. Keep the opening type translucent and make the end card solid white, so the film reads as a question becoming an answer.
- **Timing:** Big line visible from f0 (its clock t = f + 6) to f35: slide 39 f, about 35 px/f at t = 6 and 17 px/f at t = 12; letters 6 f each, 1.5 f stagger; fade over the last 7 f. No gap; small line from f36, 13 characters in 17 f, drift settled in about 40 f.
- **Use when:** The headline has a thesis word worth previewing big, in a dark, energetic launch.
- **Avoid when:** Light stages where 65% white loses contrast, or headlines longer than about 5 words whose big fragment will not read. Also avoid it when the big fragment would sit still and cropped at both edges at any point: viewers read an oversized, cropped line that vanishes and then restarts small as a false start, not a preview. It has to travel every frame it is on screen.
